sources.title: Deutsche Bank Launches Institutional Crypto Custody Service for Five Assets Including Bitcoin - BigGo Finance
passages: Deutsche Bank, Germany's largest lender, announced on November 11 that it has launched a digital asset custody service for European corporate and institutional investors.

Under the arrangement, the bank manages wallets and private keys on behalf of clients, supporting custody and third-party transfers for five assets: Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH), USDC, EURC and EURAU.
When it announced the plan in September, Deutsche Bank said it intended to provide custody and safekeeping of digital assets such as Bitcoin and Ether.

The series of moves aligns with a trend of traditional financial institutions expanding their touchpoints with the crypto market within the regulatory framework, potentially encouraging institutional capital inflows.
Gerald Podobnik, co-head of the corporate bank division, said on October 16 that the bank plans to extend custody services to financial hubs in 2027.
The move marks a further concrete step by a major European bank into the digital asset space.

extraction.body: Deutsche Bank, Germany's largest lender, announced on November 11 that it has launched a digital asset custody service for European corporate and institutional investors. Under the arrangement, the bank manages wallets and private keys on behalf of clients, supporting custody and third-party transfers for five assets: Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH), USDC, EURC and EURAU. The plan, first unveiled in September, has cleared regulatory approval and entered the operational phase. The bank's custody system combines warm and cold storage environments, protects private keys with hardware, and requires multi-person approval for transactions. Paul Maley, global head of the securities services division, said in a statement: "In the medium term, we aim to provide a fully integrated, regulatory-compliant ecosystem supporting digital asset custody, tokenization and payments." On the same day, the bank said it signed a memorandum of understanding with its majority-owned asset manager DWS (formerly DWS) to explore comprehensive commercial and technical collaboration opportunities in digital assets. The scope covers tokenized money market funds (MMFs), crypto exchange-traded commodities (ETCs) and stablecoins, with the two parties considering custody and settlement, liquidity management, treasury management and distribution using the bank's custody infrastructure. Manfred Bauer, chief product officer at DWS, said the firm plans to launch a tokenized MMF. The move marks a further concrete step by a major European bank into the digital asset space. Asia expansion is also in sight. Gerald Podobnik, co-head of the corporate bank division, said on October 16 that the bank plans to extend custody services to financial hubs in 2027. In addition to custody, it plans to offer tokenized deposits and support clients in issuing blockchain-based securities such as digital bonds. When it announced the plan in September, Deutsche Bank said it intended to provide custody and safekeeping of digital assets such as Bitcoin and Ether. The series of moves aligns with a trend of traditional financial institutions expanding their touchpoints with the crypto market within the regulatory framework, potentially encouraging institutional capital inflows. Still, custody is a business where private key management and the robustness of cybersecurity frameworks are put to the test, making post-launch operational execution the focal point. coreStoryFacts.text: Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.
German lender Deutsche Bank (NYSE: $DB) has officially launched its cryptocurrency custody service for institutional and corporate clients in Europe.
Paul Maley, Deutsche Bank's global head of trust and securities services, said custody is a first step and that the bank intends to expand into blockchain-based financial services.
Analysts say that the Binance hack has shaken investor confidence in crypto custody services provided by third parties.
Deutsche Bank has not identified its first customers or disclosed the fees its charges for holding client's digital assets.
Since then, investors, including large institutions, have pulled more than $10 billion U.S. in crypto and cash from Binance.
The new service allows customers to store and transfer Bitcoin (CRYPTO: $BTC), Ethereum (CRYPTO: $ETH) and an assortment of stablecoins through the German bank.
Deutsche Bank, Germany's largest lender, announced on November 11 that it has launched a digital asset custody service for European corporate and institutional investors.

Under the arrangement, the bank manages wallets and private keys on behalf of clients, supporting custody and third-party transfers for five assets: Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH), USDC, EURC and EURAU.
When it announced the plan in September, Deutsche Bank said it intended to provide custody and safekeeping of digital assets such as Bitcoin and Ether.

The series of moves aligns with a trend of traditional financial institutions expanding their touchpoints with the crypto market within the regulatory framework, potentially encouraging institutional capital inflows.
Gerald Podobnik, co-head of the corporate bank division, said on October 16 that the bank plans to extend custody services to financial hubs in 2027.
The move marks a further concrete step by a major European bank into the digital asset space.
Deutsche Bank announced plans to offer the service to institutional and corporate clients in Europe on Sept.
Deutsche Bank’s listing for crypto custody and transfer services in the European Union’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) register is dated Oct.
12 and names Germany’s BaFin as its regulator.
Deutsche Bank partnered with crypto infrastructure provider Taurus in 2023 to develop custody services after applying for a digital asset custody license in Germany.

passages: Deutsche Bank has launched crypto custody services for institutional clients in Europe, supporting Bitcoin, Ethereum and selected stablecoins. The bank also plans to expand into Asia in 2027 and develop tokenization and settlement services.

Deutsche Bank has officially launched its digital asset custody service for institutional and corporate clients, giving businesses in Europe a regulated way to hold and transfer cryptocurrencies through one of Germany's largest banks.

The service went live for paying clients on November 11, 2026, following the bank's September announcement. It initially supports Bitcoin, Ether, and selected stablecoins and e-money tokens, including USDC, EURC and EURAU. The launch marks another step by a major European bank into digital asset infrastructure.

Deutsche Bank's initial rollout focuses on Germany, with cross-border servicing available across Europe under applicable regulations. The bank plans to expand the offering into Asian financial centres in 2027.
Deutsche Bank will initially provide custody for five digital assets: Bitcoin, Ether, USDC, EURC and EURAU.
The service is designed for institutional investors, corporations, asset managers, hedge funds, custodians, brokers and sovereign institutions. Retail customers are not the target audience.

Under the arrangement, Deutsche Bank manages clients' digital wallets and private keys. This allows institutions to hold and transfer cryptocurrencies without having to build their own custody infrastructure.

The bank's security framework includes hardware-based private key protection, separate warm and cold storage environments, multi-person transaction approvals, segregation of responsibilities and backup and recovery arrangements.

The platform is also designed to operate within the European Union's Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) regulatory framework. Deutsche Bank lists Germany as its initial market, with cross-border servicing across Europe subject to applicable rules.

Crypto custody is only the first part of Deutsche Bank's digital asset strategy. The bank has also outlined plans to support tokenized financial instruments and expand its services toward digital asset settlement.

Paul Maley, Deutsche Bank's global head of trust and securities services, described the longer-term goal as a fully integrated, regulated ecosystem supporting the custody, tokenization and settlement of digital assets.
The bank also announced a memorandum of understanding with Deutsche Asset Management, formerly known as DWS, to explore commercial and technical cooperation in the digital asset sector.

These developments suggest that Deutsche Bank wants to move beyond simply holding cryptocurrencies for clients. Its longer-term plans could connect traditional financial services with blockchain-based assets, payments and securities.
Deutsche Bank previously said it intended to expand its digital asset custody service into Asia in 2027 after establishing the offering in Germany.

The bank has not yet identified the first Asian markets or provided a detailed rollout schedule. However, the planned expansion would bring its institutional crypto services to another major financial region.

The move follows similar developments across the banking sector. BNY, for example, recently expanded its digital asset custody platform to selected institutions in the European Union under MiCA. Its expansion shows that regulated crypto custody is becoming a growing area of competition among established financial institutions.

Altcoin Buzz previously covered BNY's expansion of regulated crypto custody to EU institutions , highlighting how traditional banks are building infrastructure for institutional digital asset adoption.

For large companies and financial institutions, holding cryptocurrencies involves more than buying Bitcoin or Ether. They also need secure key management, transaction controls, regulatory oversight and reliable infrastructure for moving assets.

A custody service from an established bank can help address some of these operational requirements. It also gives institutions an option to manage digital assets through a financial provider they may already use for traditional banking services.

However, custody does not remove the risks associated with cryptocurrencies. Digital assets remain exposed to price volatility, fraud and cyber incidents, and Deutsche Bank notes that they do not receive deposit-guarantee protection comparable to eligible bank deposits.

For now, the launch gives Deutsche Bank's institutional clients access to a limited selection of cryptocurrencies and stablecoins. The next developments to watch are the planned Asian expansion, additional supported assets and the bank's progress toward tokenization and settlement services.

extraction.body:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang speaks on stage during the Invest in Germany Summit in Berlin on Oct. 19. Lisi Niesner/Reuters Nvidia’s NVDA-Q board is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang after he had two extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday, citing people familiar with the matter. The board is preparing to meet as soon as Wednesday to determine his future, the report added. Huang’s potential departure would leave a leadership vacuum at the roughly US$4-trillion chipmaker he co-founded and built over more than three decades to become the dominant supplier of AI chips at the centre of the global artificial-intelligence boom and US-China technology rivalry. The company’s shares slid about 8 per cent in after-hours trading. Including Wednesday’s after-hours selloff, Nvidia has lost about US$600-billion in stock market value this week since the board announced its investigation. China says it doesn’t use ‘honey traps’ – but warns citizens against seductive foreign spies “Huang being removed immediately could be challenging for Nvidia since it does not have a succession plan in place ... If Mr. Huang broke the law or violated company policies, the board is likely to act as soon as they have proof,” Gil Luria, head of technology research at D.A. Davidson, said. Earlier in the day, the New York Times reported that Huang had an extramarital affair with a company executive who reported to him. The relationship was with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health care, the New York Times said, citing five people who worked at the company. When reached by phone Wednesday and asked about his relationship with Ms. Powell, Mr. Huang said, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly.” He then hung up, the New York Times reported. "Even in the event a deal is struck, an increase in flows through the waterway would still ⁠depend on mine clearance, insurance costs and whether or not shipowners would even be willing to ⁠take the risk," LSEG Oil Research said in a November 10 note. Brent futures were up US$1.22, or 1.3%, at US$92.71 a barrel by 1412 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate crude gained US$1.09, or 1.3%, to US$87.13. In the previous session, oil prices initially fell by more than US$3 a barrel after US officials played down the need for further military strikes against Iran. Prices later pared some losses after an Iranian security official said no talks were taking place between the two sides. "Oil prices are being supported by fading hopes of an imminent de-escalation," UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo said. There is little sign of attacks in the Strait of Hormuz easing after 37 ships were attacked in October, the highest monthly total since the start of the war, according to data from the Washington Institute for Near East Policy. "There has been an increase of vessel attacks in the Gulf shipping lanes amidst uncertainty of the diplomacy talks," said June Goh, a senior analyst at Sparta Commodities. She added that the key driver for the market was whether Iran would engage with US demands to reach a diplomatic agreement. Brent and West Texas Intermediate prices have fallen about 21% and 17% respectively, since the start of the month on hopes of an end to the war. A tanker was struck northeast of Lima in Oman, the UK Maritime Trade Operations agency said on Tuesday. Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy said separately on Tuesday that two tankers caught fire after hitting naval mines on an "unauthorised route" in the strait. "Even in the event a deal is struck, an increase in flows through the waterway would still depend on mine clearance, insurance costs and whether or not shipowners would even be willing to take the risk," LSEG Oil Research said in a note on Tuesday. On the supply side, US crude stocks rose by nine million barrels in the latest week, market sources said, citing data from the American Petroleum Institute. Official data is due later on Wednesday. Data from Kpler showed that Middle East crude and condensate outages had dropped to about 3.8 million barrels per day, with Saudi and Iraqi crude output back to pre-war levels and outages in both countries down significantly. Separately, Vladimir Medinsky, Russia's chief negotiator on Ukraine, said on Wednesday that a peace settlement seems to be closer after two days of talks in Abu Dhabi. A regional governor said a drone attack caused a fire in the port area of Ust-Luga on Russia's Baltic coast, injuring three workers. Russian oil refining capacity has been reduced by about 30% since late October following renewed Ukrainian drone attacks, industry sources said. Copyright © 1999- 2026 The Edge Communications Sdn. That figure was based on MSCI's earlier proposal, not the final rule. MSCI adopted a new test on October 15. Companies without substantial operating assets now count as "non-operating" and lose eligibility for its global indexes. Strategy, formerly MicroStrategy, still runs a software business. But its balance sheet is dominated by 850,364 Bitcoin, bought for $64.16 billion, according to its latest SEC filing. Japan's Metaplanet, another Bitcoin treasury firm, was also marked for deletion on MSCI's October draft list. Strategy shares closed at $122.35 on Wednesday, up 1.06%. "While not material to $MSTR, the proposal is misguided, flawed, and conflicts with established securities laws and accounting principles." The real test comes on November 30, when tracking funds must trade. JPMorgan estimated a further $8.8 billion could leave if other index providers follow MSCI. Bitcoin treasury companies sold Wall Street on one idea: stock-market access to Bitcoin. Under MSCI's rule, that model no longer counts as an operating business. MSCI will remove Strategy, the biggest company holder of Bitcoin (BTC), from its MSCI USA Index at the close of November 30. The index giant confirmed the cut in its November review filing on Wednesday, setting up a forced exit for passive fund money.

Index funds do not choose their stocks. When a company leaves the index, they must sell. JPMorgan analysts estimated last year that removal could push about $2.8 billion of Strategy shares out of these funds. That figure was based on MSCI's earlier proposal, not the final rule.
MSCI adopted a new test on October 15. Companies without substantial operating assets now count as "non-operating" and lose eligibility for its global indexes.
Strategy, formerly MicroStrategy, still runs a software business. But its balance sheet is dominated by 850,364 Bitcoin, bought for $64.16 billion, according to its latest SEC filing.
Japan's Metaplanet, another Bitcoin treasury firm, was also marked for deletion on MSCI's October draft list.
Strategy shares closed at $122.35 on Wednesday, up 1.06%. They slipped 0.85% to $121.31 in after-hours trading as the list landed.
Strategy has argued the rule does not hurt its business.
"While not material to $MSTR, the proposal is misguided, flawed, and conflicts with established securities laws and accounting principles."
The real test comes on November 30, when tracking funds must trade. JPMorgan estimated a further $8.8 billion could leave if other index providers follow MSCI.
Bitcoin treasury companies sold Wall Street on one idea: stock-market access to Bitcoin. Under MSCI's rule, that model no longer counts as an operating business.
"MSCI should be a mirror of the market, not an arbiter of it," said Michael Saylor, founder and chair of MicroStrategy.

The sources reviewed for this article do not show which names failed both filings, so Wednesday's list is the first real test.MSCI Publishes Final Deletion List Wednesday, Nov. 4 notice that it will post the review results shortly after 11:00 p.m. The notice covers MSCI's Global Standard, Small Cap, among others, and does not mention the new screen or name any company.The link to bitcoin treasury firms comes from MSCI's Oct. MSCI had first proposed excluding such firms, then dropped that plan in January 2026 and opened a broader consultation. The new test applies to any corporate issuer whose operating assets are under half of total assets, not just crypto holders.Will Strategy Be Removed From MSCI Indexes on Nov. A constituent is deleted only if it fails the screen in both of its two most recent annual filings, so Strategy must have failed on both its latest annual filing and the one before it. Unchained reports that MSCI's impact list includes Strategy, but the sources reviewed do not show the filing-by-filing results behind that placement.One detail makes the two-filing requirement a live question for Strategy. The company adopted fair-value accounting for bitcoin as of January 1, 2025, so its fiscal 2024 statements carried bitcoin at cost less impairment rather than at market value. How MSCI handles that earlier year has not been published.Constituents Face Deletion Only After Failing Both Latest Annual FilingsThe screen starts with a core test: a company passes if its operating assets exceed 50% of total assets. A company that fails it faces five ratios covering operating asset intensity, expense intensity, cash flow, fair-value exposure and dependence on outside financing, and four flags make it ineligible.Existing constituents get looser thresholds than new candidates. A constituent's operating asset intensity must fall below 10%, versus 20% for a non-constituent, and its capital dependence must exceed 30%, versus 20% for non-constituents. That makes the buffer a lookback on filings, not a waiting period. A constituent that failed both of its two latest annual filings can be deleted in the first review that applies the screen, while one that failed only the latest goes onto a public watchlist, MSCI says. Non-members are barred from joining if they fail in either period, and MSCI may use interim filings.Strategy Says Two Flags Never Trip While CoinGape Reports All FiveStrategy has fought the screen in public. 1, Executive Chairman Michael Saylor and CEO Phong Le called the proposal discriminatory, arbitrary, and misguided. The company argues that it reports its bitcoin treasury as an operating segment and books related gains and losses in operating expenses, so it trips neither the expense flag nor the fair-value flag. It also asked MSCI to place a legal hold on documents tied to the test's development, and it has announced no litigation.Analyst Adam Livingston reached a different count. He judged that Strategy likely trips operating asset intensity, expense intensity and fair-value exposure, while positive operating cash flow and financing at about 26% of assets, against the 30% constituent threshold, could let it avoid two others. Three flags would leave Strategy one short of ineligible. CoinGape, by contrast, reportedly says Strategy fails all five screens on its fiscal 2025 filings without naming a source for that count, and Decrypt's account of the same consultation does not make that claim.Strategy's own account and Livingston's cannot both be right about the expense and fair-value flags, and Unchained's report that MSCI's list includes Strategy suggests MSCI's calculation reached four flags on the data it used. That reading is an inference, since MSCI has not published the inputs. In a 2022 comment letter to the SEC, MSCI said index providers take no view on whether any investment is good or bad, and Strategy argues that deciding whether bitcoin counts as an operating asset contradicts that stance.Strategy Books Bitcoin Losses as Operating Expenses, Complicating Expense FlagStrategy's filings put bitcoin price swings inside its income statement. Since adopting fair-value accounting, it has recorded changes in bitcoin's value in net income, and for fiscal 2025 it reported a $5.40 billion unrealized loss on digital assets. Strategy told MSCI that it books bitcoin treasury gains and losses as operating expenses after discussions with the SEC, according to The Block's report.That creates the largest question the screen leaves open: the expense and fair-value flags can swing with bitcoin's price, so the same company could pass or fail depending on whether MSCI counts those fair-value lines as expenses. MSCI's published methodology, as read for this article, does not resolve how it treats them. Strategy also argues that "operating" and "non-operating" lack definitions under U.S. accounting rules, which is the same gap from another side.JPMorgan Estimated $2.8B of MSCI-Driven Selling; Others Say Far LessPassive funds that track an MSCI index must hold what it holds, so a deletion forces them to sell. JPMorgan analysts estimated in November 2025 that exclusion from MSCI indexes could cause about $2.8 billion in outflows, and another $8.8 billion if other index providers followed. The roughly $11.6 billion some outlets cite is those two figures added together.Newer estimates are lower. CoinGape put the MSCI-specific figure at $1.8 billion to $2.0 billion without saying who calculated it, and TIKR argued that funds tracking MSCI hold only about 13 million Strategy shares, less than a day's trading volume. Strategy makes up about 86.9% of the combined float-adjusted market value of the six affected companies, roughly $23.93 billion of $27.55 billion.The larger outflow scenario depends on other providers copying MSCI. FTSE Russell publishes its own Digital Asset Treasury Index Series, but the sources reviewed show no other major provider announcing an MSCI-style screen. A deletion does not delist a stock and does not force a company to sell bitcoin.Lost Issuance Premium May Cost Strategy More Than Forced SellingLivingston argues that the bigger threat is to the speed of future bitcoin accumulation, not to existing holdings.

Japan's Metaplanet, another Bitcoin treasury firm, was also marked for deletion on MSCI's October draft list.

The real test comes on November 30, when tracking funds must trade. JPMorgan estimated a further $8.8 billion could leave if other index providers follow MSCI.
Bitcoin treasury companies sold Wall Street on one idea: stock-market access to Bitcoin. Under MSCI's rule, that model no longer counts as an operating business.

A constituent is deleted only if it fails the screen in both of its two most recent annual filings, so Strategy must have failed on both its latest annual filing and the one before it. Under MSCI's latest consultation, released in August, a simulation using May 2026 data showed Strategy would be one of three companies deleted from the MSCI ACWI IMI. Metaplanet and uranium investment company Yellow Cake were the other two. SharpLink Inc (SBET), Center Laboratories and Lydia Holding would be placed on a public watchlist.MSCI's Long Fight With StrategyThe review caps a dispute from October last year, when MSCI froze any increase in the index weighting of companies whose digital assets made up 50% or more of their total assets, while it weighed excluding them. Saylor responded at the time that "index classification doesn't define us." In January, MSCI did not exclude those firms outright, and, keeping the freeze in place, said that it would run a broader review of "non-operating companies."Strategy called the final rules "discriminatory, arbitrary, and misguided" in a letter to MSCI's Equity Index Committee. The company argued that MSCI's split between operating and non-operating assets rested on terms that weren't defined under standard accounting rules. It also said the screen would hit digital asset treasury firms hardest, even though MSCI presents it as industry-neutral.Strategy asked MSCI to withdraw the rules, or revise them with clear definitions and objective criteria. It also asked MSCI to publish its consultation record and explain how it set its thresholds. The company said the change would have little effect on its business, but could hurt MSCI's reputation as a neutral index provider.How The New Rules WorkMSCI had confirmed the rules last month, calling them "minor modifications" to the August proposal. Companies will first be screened for substantial operating assets. If that fails, they will be checked against five financial ratios, and any flagged on four or more would be ineligible. To limit turnover, MSCI will remove current index members only if they fail the test in each of their two most recent annual filing periods. MSCI said it will also lift its weighting freeze on digital asset-heavy firms with the November review.Scaramucci Backs Long-Term HoldersHowever, not every investor was worried, as Anthony Scaramucci, Founder & Managing Partner of SkyBridge Capital, discussed on The Block's podcast on October 27 that Strategy rewards patience. But if you can hold that security for four or five years... you'll be incredibly well rewarded," he said.MSTR stock was up over 1% in overnight trading after closing down over 3% on Tuesday. sources.title: Ring launches flying security camera after years of delays
passages: Amazon.com Inc.’s Ring unit debuted its flying home security drone more than six years after first announcing the product, marking the brand’s belated entrance into the robotics segment.

Asked how pets have responded to the flying gadget in early tests, Siminoff said many animals tend to ignore the Drone Cam, but admitted others “don’t love it.” Ring also introduced the $1,000 Ring Rover Cam, a repurposed spin on Amazon’s earlier Astro robot that’s now dedicated to autonomous security.

An unconnected Ring Drone Cam can take off and safely land, but it depends on AI (and an active Wi-Fi connection) for nearly everything else, from setting its flight path to responding to alerts from other Ring cameras around a customer’s home.
Both products have several built-in privacy measures, and Ring said recorded videos are by default protected with “TAKE,” short for Throw Away the Key Encryption.
Ring is experimenting with other potential robotics hardware, but Siminoff said any future devices will need to have a clear purpose and solve genuine pain points for customers.
Ring ultimately decided to abandon that initial version and also scrapped a second attempt that it had been working on as recently as last year.
With this drone, he believes Ring has cracked the challenges that held back its earlier prototypes.

Users can set scheduled patrols for the device — it has built-in LED spotlights to deter burglars at night when homeowners are away — and it can automatically take to the air to investigate notifications from other products in Ring's ecosystem like sensors and alarms.
Since outdoor flight would violate Federal Aviation Administration regulations, Ring has included software precautions that will stop the drone from functioning outside.

Aside from now carrying Ring branding, the Rover Cam has received one other hardware tweak: It has a new “Light Tower” that projects a ring onto the ceiling to easily track its position when out of view.

extraction.body: Amazon.com Inc.’s Ring unit debuted its flying home security drone more than six years after first announcing the product, marking the brand’s belated entrance into the robotics segment. The new device, now called the Ring Drone Cam, will be available in late January for $250, the company said Tuesday. It has a lightweight, completely overhauled design that bears little resemblance to the drone that Ring originally announced in 2020 and aimed to ship the following year. Ring ultimately decided to abandon that initial version and also scrapped a second attempt that it had been working on as recently as last year. In both cases, Ring found itself in what Ring founder Jamie Siminoff, now a vice president at Amazon, described as “a vicious cycle.” As the company added more sensors and processing power to the drone, it needed a larger battery. The resulting increases to the product’s weight required more powerful rotors, which compromised overall flight stability. “You basically keep fixing things that then break things and make them worse,” he said at a media briefing ahead of the announcement. In an interview, Siminoff hailed Ring’s launch of the Drone Cam as a “career highlight,” acknowledging that it was a prolonged, at-times grueling effort for the brand’s engineers and designers. With this drone, he believes Ring has cracked the challenges that held back its earlier prototypes. Siminoff said a major turning point came when the company chose to heavily lean on artificial intelligence to choreograph the drone’s flying abilities and core functionality, offloading most computing needs to the cloud. An unconnected Ring Drone Cam can take off and safely land, but it depends on AI (and an active Wi-Fi connection) for nearly everything else, from setting its flight path to responding to alerts from other Ring cameras around a customer’s home. The drone is capable of flying for a maximum duration of five to eight minutes before needing to land in its base station for a battery recharge. The Ring Drone Cam’s camera has a 148-degree field of view, and video is captured at 2K resolution. Users can set scheduled patrols for the device — it has built-in LED spotlights to deter burglars at night when homeowners are away — and it can automatically take to the air to investigate notifications from other products in Ring's ecosystem like sensors and alarms. During the drone’s setup process, users will establish which zones and paths in their living space are safe for flying routes. Since outdoor flight would violate Federal Aviation Administration regulations, Ring has included software precautions that will stop the drone from functioning outside. During the media briefing, Ring showcased preproduction samples of the Drone Cam with predefined flight demonstrations, but journalists weren’t permitted to control the device directly. Asked how pets have responded to the flying gadget in early tests, Siminoff said many animals tend to ignore the Drone Cam, but admitted others “don’t love it.” Ring also introduced the $1,000 Ring Rover Cam, a repurposed spin on Amazon’s earlier Astro robot that’s now dedicated to autonomous security. The majority of hardware components inside the robot remain unchanged, Siminoff said. Amazon’s rolling Astro bot, which sold for as much as $2,350, never caught on with consumers and lacked compelling use cases. Much like Astro near the end of its lifespan, Siminoff believes the Ring Rover Cam will predominantly be used in business and manufacturing environments, conceding that it remains too expensive for most consumers — though there’s nothing stopping regular people from buying one. Aside from now carrying Ring branding, the Rover Cam has received one other hardware tweak: It has a new “Light Tower” that projects a ring onto the ceiling to easily track its position when out of view. The Rover Cam supports coverage zones as large as 5,000 square feet and, like Astro, has a periscope camera that allows for a higher perspective. Both products have several built-in privacy measures, and Ring said recorded videos are by default protected with “TAKE,” short for Throw Away the Key Encryption. When seated in its dock, the drone’s camera is switched off, and LEDs indicate when either device is recording, with an on-screen message on the Rover. Ring is experimenting with other potential robotics hardware, but Siminoff said any future devices will need to have a clear purpose and solve genuine pain points for customers. “It’s very easy to fall into the toys business when you get into robotics,” he said. “We don’t have any interest in doing that.” Welch writes for Bloomberg.

extraction.body: Ring built its reputation on a simple idea: a doorbell with a camera that lets you see who is at your front door.More than a decade later, the company is making a move that takes that original concept to a place nobody quite expected. Its latest products do not just watch; they move.Amazon Unveils Ring's AI Drone Cam For SecurityAmazon announced Ring Robotics earlier today, offering an entirely new category of Ring security products that brings autonomous, mobile devices to the home and business security market for the first time. The initial launch covers two products: Ring Drone Cam, a flying indoor security camera, and Ring Rover Cam, an autonomous ground-based robot built specifically for businesses.Ring Drone Cam is a first-of-its-kind Ring camera that flies custom routes inside a home, patrols on a set schedule, and deploys automatically when another Ring device triggers an alert. It can be sent to investigate an alarm or simply launched on demand from the Ring app at any time, giving homeowners a way to check in on specific rooms without installing cameras throughout the entire house.The drone delivers a 148-degree field of view with 360-degree rotation, capturing footage in 2K video. Two built-in LED lights activate automatically in low-light conditions so the camera remains useful after dark. When not in use, Ring Drone Cam returns to its dock and powers down with its camera off, with no recording taking place while it is docked."For years, customers told us they wanted eyes in the places a fixed camera could not reach, and peace of mind in the spots they would never want one," said Jamie Siminoff, founder and chief inventor of Ring. "The honest answer was not more cameras; it meant reimagining what a security device could be."Ring Rover Cam: Amazon Debuts On-Ground BotRing Rover Cam takes the mobile security concept to the business environment, targeting any commercial space where full camera coverage of every corner would otherwise be cost-prohibitive or logistically difficult to wire up. The robot patrols autonomously, streams in up to 4K video whenever it is in motion or on patrol, and can be deployed to any saved patrol point with a single tap from the Ring app.An adjustable periscope camera mast allows Ring Rover Cam to see over counters, shelves, and obstacles, with the height saved per stop so each patrol automatically raises or lowers to the right position for that location. When a connected Ring sensor or alarm triggers, the Rover automatically heads to its programmed patrol points to investigate without any manual input required.Built-in deterrence features include a siren and a bright light tower designed to make it unmistakably clear to anyone present that the space is monitored and protected. Two-way audio allows a manager or business owner to speak directly through the device in real time from anywhere. Person motion detection continues even when the Rover is docked, and it begins recording and alerting the moment someone enters its field of view.Ring Rover Cam is a direct descendant of Amazon's Astro home robot. The Ring team drew on feedback from Astro customers who identified roving security as the feature they valued most and built the Rover as a purpose-built security robot rather than a general home assistant that also handled security as a secondary function.Amazon's AI Pilot Powers New Ring RoboticsBoth Ring Drone Cam and Ring Rover Cam are powered by AI Pilot, a custom-built system that handles navigation, mapping, and autonomous decision-making for both devices. For Ring Drone Cam, a user carries it through the home once, and AI Pilot builds a floor plan from what the drone observes. For Ring Rover Cam, the robot explores autonomously during the initial setup period. After mapping, AI Pilot identifies rooms and suggests patrol points based on what it has learned about the layout, such as side doors, windows, storage areas, long corridors, and registers in a business setting.Privacy is a core part of the design. Ring Drone Cam does not record while docked, and its propellers are audible when in flight, making it easy to know when the device is active. Ring Rover Cam includes a Sleep Mode that retracts the periscope and turns off the microphone with a single tap, and an LED indicator on the device signals recording status at all times. All video from both devices is protected by Ring's Throw Away the Key encryption, which Amazon describes as the company's strongest default encryption standard to date.Both devices are fully integrated into the existing Ring ecosystem and are manageable through the Ring app alongside any other Ring cameras, doorbells, sensors, and alarms a customer already uses. Ring Rover Cam can also be controlled through the new Alexa Home Map, Amazon's recently announced 3D smart home interface.Frequently Asked QuestionsWhat Is Ring?Ring is a smart home security company known for its video doorbells, security cameras, and alarm systems. It was founded by Jamie Siminoff in 2013, initially launching as a Kickstarter project called Doorbot before growing into one of the most widely used home security brands in the United States and globally.The company's product lineup has expanded significantly over the years to include outdoor and indoor cameras, motion-triggered floodlights, alarm systems, solar-powered cameras, and now autonomous robotic devices through Ring Robotics.Who Owns Ring?Amazon acquired Ring in April 2018 for approximately $1 billion, making it a subsidiary of the company. Since the acquisition, Ring's product development has accelerated substantially and its integration with Amazon's Alexa ecosystem has deepened. Amazon uses Ring's security platform as a cornerstone of its broader smart home strategy, with Ring devices working natively with Alexa-powered Echo speakers, displays, and Amazon's Sidewalk network.Will These Help in Home or Business Security?Both Ring Robotics products are designed to fill specific gaps that fixed camera installations leave behind. Ring Drone Cam addresses the problem of needing visibility in rooms or areas where a permanent camera would be impractical or unwanted, letting homeowners deploy on demand rather than committing to a permanent installation.Ring Rover Cam addresses the business challenge of covering a large floor space without wiring cameras to every corner of the building, providing a mobile alternative that patrols scheduled routes, investigates alarms automatically, and streams everything in high-definition video. Both devices integrate fully with existing Ring systems, so they add to what a customer already has rather than requiring a separate app or account.When Will the New Ring Robotics Be Available?Ring Rover Cam is the first to arrive, with preorders open now and shipping beginning December 16, 2026, in the United States at a price of $999.99. Ring Drone Cam follows later, with shipping beginning January 27, 2027, at a price of $249.99.Both devices require a compatible Ring Protect plan for access to features such as scheduled patrols and video history. Ring Drone Cam has not yet been authorized by the Federal Communications Commission as required, meaning it cannot be formally offered for sale until that authorization is obtained ahead of its January 2027 ship date.

extraction.body: Amazon.com Inc.’s Ring unit debuted its flying home security drone more than six years after first announcing the product, marking the brand’s belated entrance into the robotics segment. The new device, now called the Ring Drone Cam, will be available in late January for $250, the company said Tuesday. It has a lightweight, completely overhauled design that bears little resemblance to the drone that Ring originally announced in 2020 and aimed to ship the following year. Ring ultimately decided to abandon that initial version and also scrapped a second attempt that it had been working on as recently as last year. In both cases, Ring found itself in what Ring founder Jamie Siminoff, now a vice president at Amazon, described as “a vicious cycle.” As the company added more sensors and processing power to the drone, it needed a larger battery. The resulting increases to the product’s weight required more powerful rotors, which compromised overall flight stability. “You basically keep fixing things that then break things and make them worse,” he said at a media briefing ahead of the announcement. In an interview, Siminoff hailed Ring’s launch of the Drone Cam as a “career highlight,” acknowledging that it was a prolonged, at-times grueling effort for the brand’s engineers and designers. With this drone, he believes Ring has cracked the challenges that held back its earlier prototypes. Siminoff said a major turning point came when the company chose to heavily lean on artificial intelligence to choreograph the drone’s flying abilities and core functionality, offloading most computing needs to the cloud. An unconnected Ring Drone Cam can take off and safely land, but it depends on AI (and an active Wi-Fi connection) for nearly everything else, from setting its flight path to responding to alerts from other Ring cameras around a customer’s home. The drone is capable of flying for a maximum duration of five to eight minutes before needing to land in its base station for a battery recharge. The Ring Drone Cam’s camera has a 148-degree field of view, and video is captured at 2K resolution. extraction.body: Amazon's Ring is finally bringing its long-promised flying security camera to market, but customers will have to wait a little longer before they can get one. The Ring Drone Cam was first revealed more than six years ago, yet it is only now approaching its US launch. The company announced the device on November 10, alongside a second security robot designed for businesses. However, there is one important hurdle still standing between the Ring Drone Cam and its first customers: regulatory approval.135683874Why Did Ring Take Six Years to Launch Its Security Drone?The Ring Drone Cam is not an entirely new idea. Ring first introduced the concept in September 2020 under the name Always Home Cam. At the time, the company presented it as a $249 autonomous indoor drone and expected it to arrive in 2021.That launch never happened. As TechCrunch reported at the time, the device was supposed to give homeowners a way to check areas that fixed security cameras could not easily cover. However, it remained unavailable for years.Now, Ring has brought the concept back as part of its new Ring Robotics business. The company has not explained in its announcement why the original launch took so long. The information is taken from Amazon News, Nacionale and Reuters.Why Can't You Buy the Ring Drone Cam Yet?Despite the announcement, customers cannot purchase the Ring Drone Cam immediately. Amazon says the device will begin shipping in the US on January 27, 2027, for $249.99. According to the company's notice, the drone still needs approval from the Federal Communications Commission (FCC). It cannot be sold or leased until that authorization is granted.This means the January 27 release date depends on the approval coming through in time.What Can the Ring Drone Cam Actually Do?Unlike a regular security camera, the Ring Drone Cam can move around the house. It follows preset flight routes and can also take off when a connected Ring camera, sensor or alarm detects an incident.The device uses Ring's AI Pilot system, which combines cameras, sensors, vision models and cloud processing to map indoor spaces and navigate around obstacles. It offers a 148-degree field of view, 360 degree rotation and 2K video.Scheduled flights and automatic patrols require a compatible Ring Protect plan. Amazon has not specified which plan is needed or how much it will cost.Ring's New Business Security RobotThe company also introduced Ring Rover Cam, an autonomous robot for businesses. Unlike the drone, the Rover is scheduled to ship earlier, on December 16, 2026, at $999.99.

passages: Its latest products do not just watch; they move.Amazon Unveils Ring's AI Drone Cam For SecurityAmazon announced Ring Robotics earlier today, offering an entirely new category of Ring security products that brings autonomous, mobile devices to the home and business security market for the first time.

"The honest answer was not more cameras; it meant reimagining what a security device could be."Ring Rover Cam: Amazon Debuts On-Ground BotRing Rover Cam takes the mobile security concept to the business environment, targeting any commercial space where full camera coverage of every corner would otherwise be cost-prohibitive or logistically difficult to wire up.

The initial launch covers two products: Ring Drone Cam, a flying indoor security camera, and Ring Rover Cam, an autonomous ground-based robot built specifically for businesses.Ring Drone Cam is a first-of-its-kind Ring camera that flies custom routes inside a home, patrols on a set schedule, and deploys automatically when another Ring device triggers an alert.

The robot patrols autonomously, streams in up to 4K video whenever it is in motion or on patrol, and can be deployed to any saved patrol point with a single tap from the Ring app.An adjustable periscope camera mast allows Ring Rover Cam to see over counters, shelves, and obstacles, with the height saved per stop so each patrol automatically raises or lowers to the right position for that location.

It was founded by Jamie Siminoff in 2013, initially launching as a Kickstarter project called Doorbot before growing into one of the most widely used home security brands in the United States and globally.The company's product lineup has expanded significantly over the years to include outdoor and indoor cameras, motion-triggered floodlights, alarm systems, solar-powered cameras, and now autonomous robotic devices through Ring Robotics.Who Owns Ring?Amazon acquired Ring in April 2018 for approximately $1 billion, making it a subsidiary of the company.

When not in use, Ring Drone Cam returns to its dock and powers down with its camera off, with no recording taking place while it is docked."For years, customers told us they wanted eyes in the places a fixed camera could not reach, and peace of mind in the spots they would never want one," said Jamie Siminoff, founder and chief inventor of Ring.

When a connected Ring sensor or alarm triggers, the Rover automatically heads to its programmed patrol points to investigate without any manual input required.Built-in deterrence features include a siren and a bright light tower designed to make it unmistakably clear to anyone present that the space is monitored and protected.

Since the acquisition, Ring's product development has accelerated substantially and its integration with Amazon's Alexa ecosystem has deepened.

After mapping, AI Pilot identifies rooms and suggests patrol points based on what it has learned about the layout, such as side doors, windows, storage areas, long corridors, and registers in a business setting.Privacy is a core part of the design.

extraction.body: Exclusive: Ed Miliband says sci-fi scenarios of destruction ‘now regular occurrences’, as he prepares to address Cop31 The national security of all countries is at risk from the climate crisis, as “science fiction” scenarios of widespread destruction are already coming true and economic shocks from fossil fuels are now the norm rather than the exception, the UK’s foreign secretary is to warn world leaders gathered in Turkey . Ed Miliband will tell the Cop31 UN climate summit on Wednesday that security and defence objectives are the new “frontier” of climate action, because the rapid heating of the planet will lead to food shortages, widespread economic disruption, migration and conflict. “National security is the next frontier of the fight for climate action; the scenarios once of science fiction are now regular occurrences in the daily news,” Miliband told the Guardian before his speech to world leaders and governments in Antalya . “We should be clear that climate breakdown is one of the greatest national security threats we face . Food security, threats to infrastructure, and population movements [are resulting from the climate crisis],” he said. In a veiled swipe at the Conservatives and Reform UK, which want to scrap efforts to cut greenhouse gas emissions, he added: “Those who seek to stick their heads in the sand on climate are putting our national security at risk.” Miliband arrived in Turkey on Tuesday evening for the two-day leaders’ summit segment on Wednesday and Thursday of the fortnight-long Cop31 talks, which started on Monday. Andy Burnham, the UK prime minister, is expected to travel on Wednesday for a series of bilateral meetings with fellow world leaders on Thursday. Anthony Albanese, the prime minister of Australia, and the Turkish president, Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, will open the leaders’ summit segment on Wednesday. There will also be speeches by the UN secretary general, António Guterres, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva of Brazil, which hosted last year’s Cop, and the prime minister of Ethiopia, Abiy Ahmed, who will host next year’s meeting. However, several heads of leading countries are skipping this year’s Cop , including China’s Xi Jinping, India’s Narendra Modi, France’s Emmanuel Macron and Germany’s Friedrich Merz. The European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, will attend. Miliband will argue that the world must now face the consequences of failures to cut carbon emissions over the past three decades. “It is a disaster for people and the planet, and we must reckon with its implications,” he will tell audiences at Cop31 on Wednesday. “It will drive hardship and insecurity for billions of people.” He will note that an “overshoot” of the crucial threshold of 1.5C of global heating above preindustrial levels, is now inevitable, as temperatures have exceeded that level for two years and are unlikely to subside significantly. This “overshoot” requires stronger policies to ensure heating does not accelerate, and to seek ways of returning temperatures to safer levels in decades to come. Fossil fuel shocks, such as the soaring oil price seen this year after the start of the Iran war, which has led to rampant inflation and interest rate rises from central banks in an effort to control it, will wreak further harm, according to Miliband. He told the Guardian: “A new era of global insecurity means fossil fuel shocks are now the norm – the fossil fuel rollercoaster is here to stay. First Russia, now Iran, next others, have identified global chokepoints and systemic overreliance [on fossil fuels] and the vulnerability of countries around the world that they expose.” He said the only answer was to “double down” on measures to cut greenhouse gas emissions and build resilience to the effects of extreme weather. “Next year will be the year of climate fightback, as governments, movements and communities across the world step up to defend our shared home.” Miliband will call for more investment in clean energy and efforts to use it for transport and heating, as well as urgent action to cut methane, a powerful greenhouse gas, and protect and expand forests. However, Burnham’s government is under fire in the UK for a series of recent and looming policy interventions that campaigners say will push the country off-track from its target of net zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050, and set a poor example to the rest of the world. The government plans to weaken a mandate for carmakers to ensure more of their vehicles are electric by 2030, and has given the green light to a new gasfield, Jackdaw, in the North Sea, while considering licensing a new oilfield, Rosebank , west of Shetland.

sources.title: 'What climate security means now' - Foreign Secretary at New York Climate Week - GOV.UK
passages: And my pledge to you is that the UK will pursue this national security imperative, and I see my work as Foreign Secretary as being about using our extensive embassy network, our expertise to work with others, starting here at New York Climate Week and at UNGA, at this autumn’s annual meetings at the World Bank and IMF at COP31, and in our G20 presidency next year.
Because for many years when I was the Climate Change Secretary in 2008, climate change and the destruction of nature were treated as peripheral environmental issues.
Climate and nature must be embedded in national security systems, in threat assessments, and contingency planning.
That’s why we all have a responsibility, if we care about national security, if we care about keeping our populations safe, to act as countries against the threat of the climate crisis.
Is why climate breakdown, in my view, must be an issue for foreign ministers and prime ministers, as well as energy and climate ministers.
For us as a government, clean energy, the clean energy mission, is front and centre to our economic policy, our energy security policy, and indeed our national security policy too.

extraction.body: It is really fantastic to be back here at NY Climate Week, I can honestly say to you, this is my second favourite Climate Week in the world, after London of course. I was here last year as the Energy Secretary. I’m now the Foreign Secretary of the United Kingdom, but I come here as passionate about the cause of New York Climate Week, the cause that we are all fighting for. And I want to make a simple argument to you today, which is that climate and nature loss represents an urgent national security issue and demands action equal to the scale of the challenge, and that it demands a shift in our thinking and a shift in who in government takes an interest and cares about these issues and puts them front and centre. Because for many years when I was the Climate Change Secretary in 2008, climate change and the destruction of nature were treated as peripheral environmental issues. Yes, they were seen as important, but they were separate from the core business of economic growth, or indeed energy security. And over these last two decades, the penny has dropped about the opportunity that the energy transition offers in terms of the good jobs at good wages that so many people in our different countries want to see. The national security of every country is at risk from the climate crisis , the UK 's foreign secretary, Ed Miliband , will tell world leaders at the Cop31 UN climate summit in Antalya , Turkey . Mr Miliband will say that security and defence objectives are the new "frontier" of climate action, because the rapid heating of the planet will bring food shortages , economic disruption, migration and conflict. "National security is the next frontier of the fight for climate action; the scenarios once of science fiction are now regular occurrences in the daily news," he told the Guardian before his speech. He said the climate crisis was among the biggest threats to national security. "We should be clear that climate breakdown is one of the greatest national security threats we face," Mr Miliband said. " Food security , threats to infrastructure, and population movements [are resulting from the climate crisis]," he added. He also criticised those who oppose climate action. "Those who seek to stick their heads in the sand on climate are putting our national security at risk," he said. In his speech, Mr Miliband will argue that the world must now face the consequences of failing to cut emissions over the past three decades, the Guardian reported. "It is a disaster for people and the planet, and we must reckon with its implications," he will tell the summit. "It will drive hardship and insecurity for billions of people." He will say that an overshoot of 1.5C of warming above preindustrial levels, the limit countries set in the 2015 Paris Agreement , is now inevitable, because temperatures have exceeded that level for two years and are unlikely to fall significantly. Mr Miliband will also point to the price of fossil fuels. Oil prices have soared this year after the start of the Iran war, now in its ninth month, which has disrupted shipments through the Strait of Hormuz , the narrow waterway between the Gulf and the open sea. "A new era of global insecurity means fossil fuel shocks are now the norm, the fossil fuel rollercoaster is here to stay," he told the Guardian. "First Russia , now Iran, next others, have identified global chokepoints and systemic overreliance [on fossil fuels] and the vulnerability of countries around the world that they expose." He said the answer was to "double down" on cutting greenhouse gas emissions and to build resilience to extreme weather. "Next year will be the year of climate fightback, as governments, movements and communities across the world step up to defend our shared home," he said. He will call for more investment in clean energy for transport and heating, urgent cuts to methane, a powerful greenhouse gas, and the protection and expansion of forests. The UK pledged £331 million in September to the Global Environment Facility to address instability driven by climate change and biodiversity loss. Mr Miliband urged leaders at New York Climate Week at the time to include the climate crisis in their national security assessments. Mr Miliband arrived in Turkey on Tuesday evening for the two-day leaders' segment of the fortnight-long summit, which began on Monday. Anthony Albanese , the Australian prime minister, and Recep Tayyip Erdogan , the Turkish president, will open the segment on Wednesday, with speeches from the UN secretary general, António Guterres, Brazil 's president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, whose country hosted last year's summit, and Ethiopia 's prime minister, Abiy Ahmed , whose country will host next year's. The UK prime minister, Andy Burnham , is expected to travel on Wednesday for meetings with other leaders on Thursday. China 's Xi Jinping , India 's Narendra Modi , France 's Emmanuel Macron and Germany 's Friedrich Merz are among the leaders staying away. The European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen , will attend. Campaigners say recent and planned UK policies will take the country off track from its target of net zero emissions by 2050. The government plans to weaken a mandate requiring carmakers to sell more electric vehicles by 2030, and it has approved a new gasfield in the North Sea , Jackdaw, while considering a licence for a new oilfield, Rosebank, west of Shetland . extraction.body: It is really fantastic to be back here at NY Climate Week, I can honestly say to you, this is my second favourite Climate Week in the world, after London of course. I was here last year as the Energy Secretary. I’m now the Foreign Secretary of the United Kingdom, but I come here as passionate about the cause of New York Climate Week, the cause that we are all fighting for. And I want to make a simple argument to you today, which is that climate and nature loss represents an urgent national security issue and demands action equal to the scale of the challenge, and that it demands a shift in our thinking and a shift in who in government takes an interest and cares about these issues and puts them front and centre. Because for many years when I was the Climate Change Secretary in 2008, climate change and the destruction of nature were treated as peripheral environmental issues. Yes, they were seen as important, but they were separate from the core business of economic growth, or indeed energy security. And over these last two decades, the penny has dropped about the opportunity that the energy transition offers in terms of the good jobs at good wages that so many people in our different countries want to see. And Russia’s invasion of Ukraine underlined the dependence that so many countries face on fossil fuel markets, the fossil fuel roller coaster, as we call it in the UK. And I think people now see the energy security imperative, the energy independence imperative of clean energy. But having understood the jobs opportunity and the energy security imperative, my argument to you today is: we need to take the next step and recognize the national security imperative too. Over 150 million hectares burned globally in the first four months of 2026 alone. Nepal’s devastating floods happening due to glacial collapse and the coming El Nino, as Prime Minister Albanese said, is already forecast to be the strongest in living memory. And the nature loss crisis is just as acute, with ecosystems being degraded in every region of the world. That is the conclusion of the UK’s recent nature security assessment, which you can all read. Is why climate breakdown, in my view, must be an issue for foreign ministers and prime ministers, as well as energy and climate ministers. The security community, not just the activist community, the generals, not just the green campaigners. Climate and nature must be embedded in national security systems, in threat assessments, and contingency planning. Countries need to pool information because a shock beginning in one country can rapidly travel through supply chains, financial markets, and migration patterns to other countries. These shocks that cross borders, better forecasting and early warning systems, more resilient infrastructure, health and food systems, more effective disaster risk finance and insurance. Acting before the crisis hits, rather than simply picking up the pieces afterwards. That’s why we all have a responsibility, if we care about national security, if we care about keeping our populations safe, to act as countries against the threat of the climate crisis. We recently announced our intention to invest £400 million in the Tropical Forest Forever facility to support international action to protect tropical forests. For us as a government, clean energy, the clean energy mission, is front and centre to our economic policy, our energy security policy, and indeed our national security policy too. And my pledge to you is that the UK will pursue this national security imperative, and I see my work as Foreign Secretary as being about using our extensive embassy network, our expertise to work with others, starting here at New York Climate Week and at UNGA, at this autumn’s annual meetings at the World Bank and IMF at COP31, and in our G20 presidency next year. When I left the Copenhagen climate summit, which didn’t go so well for those of you from your memories, in in 2009 we were heading for a four degree world. Which is we know the scale of the problem, it’s not some theoretical future thing that might happen as it was 20 years ago, we see the climate crisis unfolding, but we have time to do something about it. And finally, we will do this, in my view, because I believe that actually countries all around the world now recognize this threat, and they recognize that we can only solve it acting together. Last year, when I was here, I said, “don’t give up on multilateralism”, and I think the countries across the world are not giving up on multilateralism. So many countries, I mean, so many foreign ministers and others, I mean, know that no country can tackle climate change on its own, but we can do it together. So, friends, this is about what makes our country safe. This is about what makes our economies strong, and this is about what will sustain our planet and our people for future generations to come.

The national security of every country is at risk from the climate crisis , the UK 's foreign secretary, Ed Miliband , will tell world leaders at the Cop31 UN climate summit in Antalya , Turkey .

Mr Miliband will say that security and defence objectives are the new "frontier" of climate action, because the rapid heating of the planet will bring food shortages , economic disruption, migration and conflict.
"National security is the next frontier of the fight for climate action; the scenarios once of science fiction are now regular occurrences in the daily news," he told the Guardian before his speech.
He said the climate crisis was among the biggest threats to national security.

"We should be clear that climate breakdown is one of the greatest national security threats we face," Mr Miliband said. " Food security , threats to infrastructure, and population movements [are resulting from the climate crisis]," he added.
He also criticised those who oppose climate action. "Those who seek to stick their heads in the sand on climate are putting our national security at risk," he said.
In his speech, Mr Miliband will argue that the world must now face the consequences of failing to cut emissions over the past three decades, the Guardian reported.
"It is a disaster for people and the planet, and we must reckon with its implications," he will tell the summit. "It will drive hardship and insecurity for billions of people."

He will say that an overshoot of 1.5C of warming above preindustrial levels, the limit countries set in the 2015 Paris Agreement , is now inevitable, because temperatures have exceeded that level for two years and are unlikely to fall significantly.

Mr Miliband will also point to the price of fossil fuels. Oil prices have soared this year after the start of the Iran war, now in its ninth month, which has disrupted shipments through the Strait of Hormuz , the narrow waterway between the Gulf and the open sea.

"A new era of global insecurity means fossil fuel shocks are now the norm, the fossil fuel rollercoaster is here to stay," he told the Guardian. "First Russia , now Iran, next others, have identified global chokepoints and systemic overreliance [on fossil fuels] and the vulnerability of countries around the world that they expose."
He said the answer was to "double down" on cutting greenhouse gas emissions and to build resilience to extreme weather.

"Next year will be the year of climate fightback, as governments, movements and communities across the world step up to defend our shared home," he said. He will call for more investment in clean energy for transport and heating, urgent cuts to methane, a powerful greenhouse gas, and the protection and expansion of forests.

The UK pledged £331 million in September to the Global Environment Facility to address instability driven by climate change and biodiversity loss. Mr Miliband urged leaders at New York Climate Week at the time to include the climate crisis in their national security assessments.

Mr Miliband arrived in Turkey on Tuesday evening for the two-day leaders' segment of the fortnight-long summit, which began on Monday. Anthony Albanese , the Australian prime minister, and Recep Tayyip Erdogan , the Turkish president, will open the segment on Wednesday, with speeches from the UN secretary general, António Guterres, Brazil 's president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, whose country hosted last year's summit, and Ethiopia 's prime minister, Abiy Ahmed , whose country will host next year's. The UK prime minister, Andy Burnham , is expected to travel on Wednesday for meetings with other leaders on Thursday.

China 's Xi Jinping , India 's Narendra Modi , France 's Emmanuel Macron and Germany 's Friedrich Merz are among the leaders staying away. The European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen , will attend.

Campaigners say recent and planned UK policies will take the country off track from its target of net zero emissions by 2050. The government plans to weaken a mandate requiring carmakers to sell more electric vehicles by 2030, and it has approved a new gasfield in the North Sea , Jackdaw, while considering a licence for a new oilfield, Rosebank, west of Shetland .

extraction.body: Nabu Casa — the commercial side of the Open Home Foundation, which runs Home Assistant — just launched the Home Assistant Connect Aux-2, a multi-function box designed to help you bring more non-smart devices into your smart home. It’s part of Home Assistant’s ongoing efforts to become more user-friendly. I’ve been testing the Aux-2 for a couple days and I’ve found it unsurprisingly useful and surprisingly easy to set up. The Aux-2 is a $69 box about the size of a deck of cards. Its USB port lets you plug in a Nabu Casa Z-Wave or Zigbee antenna in case your Home Assistant hub isn’t in a good spot. And you can connect an amplifier or powered speakers to its audio jack to stream music to older audio equipment. All of these things leverage Home Assistant’s capabilities as an open-source platform. The Aux-2 is based on ESPHome, an open platform for making DIY smart home devices from cheap, flexible ESP boards, and it uses existing Home Assistant/ESPHome integrations for all its features. The serial integration was developed earlier this year; Music Assistant and SendSpin, which power the audio-out feature, are in active development. I have a Home Assistant install, but even after several years it is not my primary smart home platform simply because of friction and time constraints. Instead, I have a hodgepodge of Google Home, Apple Home, and a few devices that are only in Home Assistant. But the Aux-2’s capabilities perfectly intersect with two things I’d been meaning to do anyway, one of which I’m already using Home Assistant for. First, I have a garage fridge, because I live in Texas. I also have children, which means sometimes the fridge or freezer door gets left open. A couple years ago, I set up a few Aqara temperature sensors, connected to Home Assistant via a now-discontinued Zigbee dongle, and set up an automation to alert me if the fridge or freezer get too warm. But they frequently drop connection (probably because they’re inside a fridge in the garage), they chew through coin cell batteries, and they have no displays, which means I also have a cheap Acu-rite hygrometer in the fridge so I can see the temperature without pulling out my phone. Someone tipped me off to Govee’s Bluetooth hygrometers, but I’d need a Bluetooth proxy to get them into Home Assistant. I also have a set of in-wall speakers in my living room that I’ve never used. Do I try to get them to work with my four Sonos speakers? Setting up the Aux-2 was much easier than I expected. Mercifully, they maintained their Bluetooth connection through three walls and a fridge, and now my fridge monitoring setup works again. The audio capability took a little longer, but most of that was spent hooking the speakers up to the amp I ended up buying and setting up Music Assistant, which I didn’t have installed. Music Assistant lives on your Home Assistant hardware and can play from many different services — from Spotify to YouTube Music to local files and more — and to many different outputs, like Sonos, Wiim, AirPlay, Google Cast, and others, but they all need to be configured, and that took a beat. I can now play music to the in-wall speakers using Music Assistant. Sendspin, the whole-home audio standard (also developed by the Open Home Foundation) is supposed to be able to let you group speakers from different protocols under certain conditions, but I haven’t gotten that working yet. The Aux-2 doesn’t do anything you couldn’t do already with an ESP32 board and various accessories, or even other ESP-based devices. The Apollo Automations Cast-1, for example, costs $35 and supports the same music-casting and Bluetooth proxy features I’m actually using from the Aux-2 at the moment. You could bodge together something even cheaper with DIY parts. Both Nabu Casa and Apollo fund the Open Home Foundation, which develops Home Assistant and ESPHome (and Sendspin and Music Assistant), and both provide hardware that’s a little easier to use than DIY options. I bought a three-pack of ESP32 boards for $16 three years ago. But now that I’ve used the Aux-2 and dipped my toe into the ESPHome waters, maybe I will.

passages: Home Assistant works with a huge number of smart home devices, but it doesn't work with everything.
The first is to see if the device is automatically discovered.
Power the device on and ensure it's connected, and you may find that it appears in Home Assistant's list of discovered devices.
Support may have arrived since the last time you checked.
This doesn't include custom components that you can install via HACS that are not officially supported integrations.
Home Assistant also has mature support for Matter, and continues to add new Matter features.
If you have Matter devices, Home Assistant is a great way to connect and control them.
In the past, to do so, you needed to use manual workarounds or custom integrations, but Home Assistant now has a dedicated native platform for infrared control.
However, you can also use ESP32 devices as Bluetooth proxies and place them near your Bluetooth devices.

Currently, there's only an LG Infrared integration that will let you control an LG straight out of the box, but for other IR devices, you can use the remote.learn_command action to learn the commands that your remote sends out, and the remote.send_command action to send these commands from your IR proxy.
It means that in theory, you can add almost any IR device that uses a remote to Home Assistant.
